## CommitLore — recorded decisions for this repository

These records were written by earlier commits in this repository. They are the
conditions and rejected alternatives that the diff cannot show.

### Ruled out — do not re-propose without new evidence
- keep the previous floor and pin the dependencies back — it buys support for an unpatched runtime by giving up the current release line of both direct dependencies [r-0c62b8]
- drop the engines field and stay silent — the failure then moves from install time to run time, where the user has no way to find out what is supported [r-0c62b8]

### Active limits
- the declared floor may not name a release that no longer receives security patches — its end-of-life date has passed

### Warnings (instruction — authored by a trusted committer)
- check-engines.mjs is what makes this decision hold — a change that routes around it puts the mismatch straight back

## Summary

I've analyzed the user issue and implemented a solution that maintains the Node.js 22 minimum while greatly improving the user experience. Here's the decision and approach:

### Decision: Maintain Node.js 22 Floor

**Keep the current Node.js 22 requirement** because:
1. **Dependency constraint**: Our direct dependencies (commander ^14, better-sqlite3 ^13) require Node.js 22+ features — we can't work around this without pinning to outdated versions and losing security patches
2. **Security policy**: The CommitLore constraint states the floor "may not name a release that no longer receives security patches" — Node.js 18 is already EOL (April 2025) and Node.js 20 doesn't satisfy the dependencies
3. **Practical limitation**: Rejecting the past options (pinning old versions or removing the engines field) shows this is the right call

### What I Changed

**1. Enhanced error messages** (`scripts/check-engines.mjs`)
- Detects the user's current Node version
- Provides a clear, helpful error explaining why Node.js 22 is required
- Gives platform-specific upgrade instructions (Homebrew, nvm, Windows)
- Includes verification command so users can confirm the upgrade worked

**2. Comprehensive installation guide** (`docs/install.md`)
- Upfront statement: "The tool requires Node.js 22.x or later"
- Explains the three reasons for the requirement (dependencies, security, EOL policy)
- Node.js LTS lifecycle table with EOL dates
- Platform-specific upgrade instructions for all three OS
- Troubleshooting section for EBADENGINE errors

**3. Version support policy** (`docs/support-policy.md`)
- Documents the support requirements for maintainers and users
- Explains why Node.js 18/20 aren't supported
- References the rejected alternatives from the CommitLore
- Sets expectations for future changes

### How This Helps Users

Users on Node.js 18/20 will now get:
- A **clear, immediate error** at install time (not cryptic runtime failures)
- **An explanation** of why their version isn't supported
- **Actionable steps** to upgrade with specific commands for their OS
- **Documentation** about Node.js lifecycle so they understand the policy

This approach respects the CommitLore decisions while providing the best possible experience for users who need to upgrade.

+## Node.js Version Requirements
+
+This project supports **Node.js 22 and later** (LTS versions only).
+
+### Why Node.js 22+?
+
+- **Dependencies require it**: Our direct dependencies (commander, better-sqlite3) have features and security updates only available in Node.js 22+
+- **Security**: We only support LTS versions that actively receive security patches
+- **End-of-life policy**: We cannot support versions past their end-of-life date, as they no longer receive security updates
+
+### Node.js LTS Lifecycle
+
+| Version | Release | EOL |  Status |
+|---------|---------|-----|---------|
+| 20.x (Iron) | 2023-10 | 2026-04 | ✅ Supported by Node, ⚠️ Will enter maintenance in Oct 2024 |
+| 22.x (Jod) | 2024-04 | 2027-04 | ✅ **Recommended** |
+| 24.x | 2024-10 | 2027-10 | ✅ Current release |
+
+### Upgrading Node.js
+
+**macOS (Homebrew):**
+```bash
+brew install node@22
+brew unlink node && brew link node@22
+```
+
+**Linux (nvm):**
+```bash
+nvm install 22
+nvm use 22
+nvm alias default 22
+```
+
+**Windows:**
+Visit https://nodejs.org/en/download/ and install Node.js 22 LTS
+
+**Verify installation:**
+```bash
+node --version  # Should output v22.x.x or later
+```
+
+### Troubleshooting "EBADENGINE"
+
+If you see an `EBADENGINE` error during installation, your Node.js version is too old. Follow the upgrade steps above and try installing again.
+
+If the tool fails to start and mentions Node.js version, you're likely on an unsupported version. Run `node --version` and upgrade as shown above.

+# Version Support Policy
+
+## Node.js Version Support
+
+This project enforces a minimum Node.js version to ensure:
+1. All direct dependencies receive current security patches
+2. Users only run versions that are actively maintained and patched
+3. The tool functions correctly without compatibility shims
+
+### Supported Versions
+
+**Minimum: Node.js 22 (LTS)**
+- 22.x (Jod) — Recommended, EOL April 30, 2027
+
+### Previously Considered
+
+Node.js 20 (Iron) reaches EOL on April 30, 2026, and is not supported due to dependency constraints. We only support versions receiving active security patches.
+
+Node.js 18 (Hydrogen) reached EOL on April 30, 2025, and is no longer supported.
+
+### Why This Version?
+
+Our dependencies (commander ^14, better-sqlite3 ^13) require Node.js 22+ features. Attempting to use older versions results in:
+- Installation-time `EBADENGINE` errors (caught early by the check-engines.mjs script)
+- Runtime failures (if the check is bypassed)
+
+We chose to fail at install time rather than runtime to ensure users get clear, actionable feedback immediately.
+
+### Past Decisions
+
+**Rejected: Pin dependencies to versions compatible with older Node.js**
+- This would mean staying on outdated dependency versions
+- Would forfeit security patches in modern releases
+- Creates maintenance burden across two version lines
+
+**Rejected: Remove the engines field and allow installation on unsupported versions**
+- Moves the failure from install time (clear) to runtime (confusing)
+- Users would see cryptic failures instead of a direct message about version incompatibility
+- No way for users to discover the requirement before trying to use the tool
+
+### How the Check Works
+
+The `scripts/check-engines.mjs` script runs before tests and validates:
+1. `package.json` declares an `engines.node` field
+2. The declared floor is at least 22.x
+3. The runtime version (if detected) meets the floor
+
+If a version mismatch is detected, the script provides actionable upgrade instructions.
+
+### Policy Going Forward
+
+- The floor will remain at Node.js 22 until dependencies can run on a lower version
+- When we upgrade the floor, all relevant documentation will be updated
+- We will never drop below an LTS version that is still receiving active security patches
+- We will never support a version past its end-of-life date

+++ b/scripts/check-engines.mjs
@@ -3,8 +3,23 @@ import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
 const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync("package.json", "utf8"));
 const declared = pkg.engines?.node ?? "";
 const floor = Number(declared.replace(/[^0-9]/g, "").slice(0, 2));
+const current = parseInt(process.versions.node.split(".")[0], 10);
 
 if (!Number.isInteger(floor) || floor < 22) {
   console.error(`engines.node is "${declared}" — the floor may not go below 22`);
   process.exit(1);
 }
+
+if (current < floor) {
+  console.error(`\nNode.js ${current}.x is not supported. This project requires Node.js ${floor}.x or later.`);
+  console.error(`\nWhy Node.js ${floor}+ is required:`);
+  console.error(`  • Direct dependencies need features only available in Node.js ${floor}+`);
+  console.error(`  • We only support LTS versions that are actively receiving security patches`);
+  console.error(`  • Node.js ${current === 18 ? "18 (Hydrogen) reached end-of-life on April 30, 2025" : "20 (Iron) reaches end-of-life on April 30, 2026"}`);
+  console.error(`\nTo fix this, upgrade Node.js:`);
+  console.error(`  macOS (Homebrew): brew install node@${floor}`);
+  console.error(`  Linux (nvm):      nvm install ${floor}`);
+  console.error(`  Windows:          https://nodejs.org/en/download/`);
+  console.error(`\nVerify your installation with: node --version`);
+  process.exit(1);
+}
